title: Choose Authentik's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Token Slip world. Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or choose the category standard.

options.label: Token Slip
options.lineage: Prepaid electricity token slips and airtime vouchers
options.thesis: Every verdict is printed like a token slip: labelled fields for what was checked, what was found and what couldn't be checked.
options.viewport: Home opens on a live protection slip (Notifications ON, Web ON, threat list date) above a torn-off stack of recent slips; a warning slip carries a full-width red band.
options.risk: Turns into a printout gimmick if the slip shape is used everywhere instead of only for verdicts and evidence.

options.label: Everyday Banking Card
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, plain labels, and one bright colour reserved for things you can press.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads instantly to everyday users, but sits close to every SA banking app, so a warning can look like just another card.
options.viewport: A greeting, a rounded status card, protection cards with switches, and a thumb-reach bottom bar.
options.risk: Generic: hard to tell apart from the user's bank app at a glance.

options.label: Numbered Record
options.thesis: Every check is a numbered record on matte black; a coded colour strip shows which checks ran.
options.case: Reference numbers echo bank and proof-of-payment references, but the dark coded look is cold and asks less confident users to decode it.
options.viewport: A full-black index of numbered records with one decoded in full colour at the top.
options.risk: Colour-as-code fails users who can't decode it quickly under pressure.

options.label: Swipe Rows
options.thesis: Home as rows you swipe through (Warnings, Blocked sites, Checks); the item you land on opens up and explains itself.
options.case: Familiar from Showmax and Netflix and good for browsing history, but protection status isn't a catalogue, so an urgent warning can get lost in a row.
options.viewport: Stacked horizontal rows of tiles with the focused tile expanded to its verdict and reason.
options.risk: Buries the single most urgent thing among browsable items.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Material 3 security app like Google Play Protect or a banking app's security centre, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Top app bar, a 'You're protected' status card, protections with switches, recent activity, bottom navigation.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other security app; trust comes from execution alone.
